name: Story of an Era
description: A history or social-science narrative: a hook, a timeline, causes and consequences, a point to debate, and a check. Dates only from the source or well-established.
audience: Teaching events, movements and eras in order.

signals.why: your words are about events over time
the topic has causes and effects

slides.guidance: Lesson title for {topic} and a short subtitle that names the class level.
A striking fact, date or question that opens {topic}.

variants.guidance: A classroom meme about {topic}. Pick one format from MEME FORMATS that matches the idea, write captions a {grade} student finds funny and that make the correct idea easier to remember. Kind to students, never about a person.

slides.guidance: Students will be able to explain what happened in {topic} and why.
The key events of {topic} in order, with dates. Only dates in the source or firmly established.
The causes that led to the central event of {topic}, and its effects.
Why people at the time acted as they did, in a few clear points.
One or two open questions that ask students to judge or connect, not recall.
Takeaways: what happened, why, and what changed.
